coverage.topic: Unwinding of yen carry trades following Bank of Japan rate hikes can trigger forced liquidation of overseas assets and stocks regardless of underlying business fundamentals.

Good companies can experience short-term selling when holders face liquidity demands and margin pressures, meaning price drops often stem from external capital flows rather than fundamental changes in business operations.

The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, which was largely priced in and led to a weaker yen, averting the disruptive shock that an unexpected 50 basis point hike would have had on the carry trade.
U.S. equities rebounded as energy costs and long-term rates eased, showing that continued earnings growth can coexist with valuation compression during a more grinding, protracted market advance.
